Definition: to drag off roughly; by implication, to bring up the cud (i.e. ruminate); by analogy, to saw
BiblicalUsage: Garar means to drag off roughly, and by the same motion, to chew the cud and to saw. The costly stones of the temple were sawed with saws in 1 Kings 7:9, and the fishermen drag their catch in the net in Habakkuk 1:15. The swine chews not the cud in Leviticus 11:7, and the robbery of the wicked shall destroy them in Proverbs 21:7, because they drag away what is not theirs.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe dragging is the motion of both work and wickedness. The saw drags through stone to build God's house, and the wicked drag away their neighbour's goods. I hold that the difference is not the motion but the master.
